lesson.subtitle: Lesson 3 -- The Hospital Project
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Luciana Galleote Cartocci | Lesson 3 -- The Hospital Project
lesson.grammar_point: past simple (regular and irregular) with sequencers to tell a project story

listenings.text: Two years ago we moved the data center of a large hospital in Bangalore. The hospital gave us one weekend, from Saturday night to Monday morning. First, we tested everything in the new room for two weeks. Then, on Saturday at ten in the evening, we started the move. At two in the morning we ran into a problem. One of the new servers did not start. For one hour nobody spoke. Then an engineer found a workaround: we used an old server for that system until Tuesday. In the end, the new data center went live at six on Monday morning, one hour before the deadline. The doctors did not notice anything.

Last year our hospital in Lyon bought four hundred new cameras. The plan was simple: eight weeks, from the site survey to the handover. But in the third week we had a setback. The cameras arrived five weeks late, because of a problem at the factory. I was very worried. Our partner did something intelligent. While we waited, they installed all the cabling, floor by floor. So when the cameras finally arrived, the installation took only one week. We did not finish on schedule, but we lost only two weeks, not five. And at the handover they trained forty people from my security team.

I will never forget the night our access control system went live in a hospital in Chicago. We chose a Sunday night, because the hospital had the fewest visitors on Sunday nights. We started at eleven. We changed three hundred doors, one by one, and we tested every door two times. At five in the morning the day team arrived. The first nurse walked to the door of the emergency room, used her new badge, and the door opened. We all started to laugh. It was a very small moment, but it meant months of work. Before we went home, we wrote a short report of the night for the hospital, and then we slept all day.
